--- title: "Multi-species occupancy models" subtitle: WILD(FISH) 8390
Inference for Models of Fish and Wildlife Population Dynamics
## author: "Richard Chandler" ## date: "2025-11-18" format: revealjs: theme: default embed-resources: false css: ../../custom.css toc: false toc-depth: 2 toc-title: Outline code-fold: false echo: true description: | Two-species and community occupancy models --- # Overview {visibility="hidden"} # Two-species models # Community occupancy models ## Community occupancy model Species may go undetected for a couple reason: ::: {.incremental} 1. They are rare and are not present in our sample. 2. They are present in our sample but are cryptic. :::
::: {.fragment} Older methods like rarefaction attempt to address the first issue but not the second. ::: ::: {.fragment} We have to address both issues to obtain unbiased estimates of community parameters like species richness. ::: ## Community occupancy model ::: {style='font-size: 75%;'} Occupancy of species $i$ present at site $j$: $$ z_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_i) $$ ::: {.fragment} Detection data for species $i$ at site $j$ on occasion $k$: $$ y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_{ij} \times p_i) $$ :::
::: {.fragment} Species-specific parameters can be modeled as functions of covariates and/or regarded as random effects. Here's an example without covariates: $$ \mathrm{logit}(\psi_j) \sim \mathrm{Norm}(\mu_{\psi}, \sigma^2_{\psi}) $$ $$ \mathrm{logit}(p_j) \sim \mathrm{Norm}(\mu_{p}, \sigma^2_{p}) $$ ::: ::: ## Species richness ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} What do we do if we don't know how many species are in the community? ::: {.fragment} Two options: ::: ::: {.fragment} 1. Model only the species that were in the sample. * This won't let you estimate actual richness, but it will let you account for species (in the sample) that were present but not detected at some sites. ::: ::: {.fragment} 2. Estimate the number of species that were *not* detected in the sample. * This can be accomplished using data augmentation. * Ideally, we would use some sort of "species checklist" to focus on species that *could have been present*. ::: ::: ## Simulation without covariates ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1-3|5-9|11-14|16-24"} N <- 50 # n_species J <- 40 # n_sites K <- 3 # n_visits ## Occupancy as logit-normal random effects set.seed(34020) mu_logit_psi <- -2 sd_logit_psi <- 1 psi <- plogis(rnorm(n=N, mean=mu_logit_psi, sd=sd_logit_psi)) ## Detection prob as logit-normal random effects mu_logit_p <- -1 sd_logit_p <- 0.5 p <- plogis(rnorm(n=N, mean=mu_logit_p, sd=sd_logit_p)) ## Occupancy and data z <- matrix(NA, nrow=N, ncol=J) # latent occupancy state for species i at site j yall <- array(NA, dim=c(N,J,K)) # Data (except we don't know spp that weren't detected) for(i in 1:N) { z[i,] <- rbinom(n=J, size=1, prob=psi[i]) for(j in 1:J) { yall[i,j,] <- rbinom(n=K, size=1, prob=z[i,j]*p[i]) } } ``` ::: ::: ## Simulation without covariates ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hist(psi, xlab="Species-level occupancy (psi)", cex.lab=1.5, main="") hist(p, xlab="Species-level detection probability (p)", cex.lab=1.5, main="") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-multi-spp-occu_files/figure-revealjs/psi-re-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: ## Simulation without covariates ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Some species were not detected, and thus can't be part of the dataset. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} detected <- rowSums(yall)>0 table(detected) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` detected FALSE TRUE 5 45 ``` ::: ::: We discard them like so: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y <- yall[detected,,] # Discard species that weren't detected ``` ::: ::: ## JAGS model pretending we know all the species ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { mu_logit_psi ~ dnorm(0, 1) sd_logit_psi ~ dexp(1) mu_logit_p ~ dnorm(0, 1) sd_logit_p ~ dexp(1) for(i in 1:n_species) { logit_psi[i] ~ dnorm(mu_logit_psi, 1/sd_logit_psi^2) logit_p[i] ~ dnorm(mu_logit_p, 1/sd_logit_p^2) psi[i] <- ilogit(logit_psi[i]) p[i] <- ilogit(logit_p[i]) for(j in 1:n_sites) { z[i,j] ~ dbern(psi[i]) for(k in 1:n_occasions) { y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(z[i,j]*p[i]) } } } } ``` ::: ::: ## JAGS model pretending we know all the species ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} library(jagsUI) jd_fixedN <- list(y=y, n_species=nrow(y), n_sites=ncol(y), n_occasions=dim(y)[3]) jp_fixedN <- c("mu_logit_psi", "sd_logit_psi", "mu_logit_p", "sd_logit_p") ji_fixedN <- function() list(mu_logit_psi=rnorm(1), sd_logit_psi=rexp(1), mu_logit_p=rnorm(1), sd_logit_p=rexp(1), z=matrix(1, nrow=nrow(y), ncol=ncol(y))) post_fixedN <- jags.basic(data=jd_fixedN, inits=ji_fixedN, parameters.to.save=jp_fixedN, model.file="comm-occ-knownN.jag", n.chains=1, n.iter=2000) plot(post_fixedN) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-multi-spp-occu_files/figure-revealjs/jags-fit-knownN-1.png){fig-align='center' width=50%} ::: ::: ::: ## Expanding the model to estimate richness
We can use data augmentation to infer how many species were missed, and thus estimate the size of the entire community. ::: {.fragment}
Here's the expanded part of the model: $$ w_i \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\Omega) \\ z_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(w_i \times \psi_{i}) $$ ::: ## JAGS model estimating richness ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { mu_logit_psi ~ dnorm(0, 1) sd_logit_psi ~ dexp(1) mu_logit_p ~ dnorm(0, 1) sd_logit_p ~ dexp(1) omega ~ dunif(0,1) for(i in 1:M) { w[i] ~ dbern(omega) logit_psi[i] ~ dnorm(mu_logit_psi, 1/sd_logit_psi^2) logit_p[i] ~ dnorm(mu_logit_p, 1/sd_logit_p^2) psi[i] <- ilogit(logit_psi[i]) p[i] <- ilogit(logit_p[i]) for(j in 1:n_sites) { z[i,j] ~ dbern(w[i]*psi[i]) for(k in 1:n_occasions) { y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(z[i,j]*p[i]) } } } N <- sum(w) # Species richness } ``` ::: ::: ## JAGS model estimating richness ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center" output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} M <- 100 # Augment to M=100 possible species y_aug <- array(0, c(M,J,K)) y_aug[1:nrow(y),,] <- y # Insert observed data jd_unknownN <- list(y=y_aug, M=M, n_sites=ncol(y), n_occasions=dim(y)[3]) jp_unknownN <- c("mu_logit_psi", "sd_logit_psi", "mu_logit_p", "sd_logit_p", "N") ji_unknownN <- function() list(mu_logit_psi=rnorm(1), sd_logit_psi=0.1, mu_logit_p=rnorm(1), sd_logit_p=0.1, w=rep(1, M), z=matrix(1, nrow=M, ncol=ncol(y))) post_unknownN <- jags.basic(data=jd_unknownN, inits=ji_unknownN, parameters.to.save=jp_unknownN, model.file="comm-occ-unknownN.jag", n.chains=1, n.iter=5000) ``` ::: ::: ## JAGS model estimating richness ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-multi-spp-occu_files/figure-revealjs/jags-mcmc-unkownN-1-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-multi-spp-occu_files/figure-revealjs/jags-mcmc-unkownN-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Additional community parameters We can use the $z$ matrix to estimate community parameters other than richness, including evenness, similarity, diversity, etc... Jaccard similarity index comparing sites: $$ S_{j,j'} = \frac{\sum z_j z_{j'}}{\sum z_j + \sum z_{j'} - \sum z_j z_j'} $$

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
